text: Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit in the wilderness,
where for forty days he was tempted by the devil. He ate nothing during those days, and when they were over, he was hungry.
The devil said to him, "If you are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread."
Jesus answered him, "It is written: 'Man shall not live by bread alone.'"
Then the devil led him up and showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a single moment,
and said to him, "I will give you all this authority and their glory, for it has been handed over to me, and I give it to anyone I please.
So if you will bow down before me, it will all be yours."
Jesus answered him, "It is written: 'You shall worship the Lord your God, and him alone shall you serve.'"
Then he took him to Jerusalem and set him on the pinnacle of the temple, and said to him, "If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here.
For it is written: 'He will command his angels concerning you, to guard you,'
and, 'On their hands they will lift you up, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.'"
Jesus answered him, "It is said: 'You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.'"
When the devil had finished every temptation, he left him until another time.
Then Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit to Galilee, and news about him spread through the whole surrounding region.
He taught in their synagogues, and everyone praised him.
He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and on the Sabbath day he went into the synagogue, as was his custom, and stood up to read.
The scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him, and unrolling it he found the place where it was written:

"The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim release to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to set free those who are crushed,
to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor."
Then he rolled up the scroll, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down. Every eye in the synagogue was fixed on him.
He began to speak to them: "Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing."

versions.text: He began by saying to them, "Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing."
versions.explanation: "He began by saying" implies this was merely the first of several statements; the Greek simply marks the start of his address.

text: They all spoke well of him and marveled at the gracious words that came from his mouth. And they said, "Isn't this Joseph's son?"
So he said to them, "No doubt you will quote me this proverb: 'Doctor, heal yourself.' You will say, 'Do here in your hometown what we have heard you did in Capernaum.'
Truly I tell you," he went on, "no prophet is accepted in his hometown.
In truth I tell you, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three years and six months and a severe famine came over the whole land.
Yet Elijah was sent to none of them, but to a widow in Zarephath in the region of Sidon.
And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of the prophet Elisha, yet not one of them was cleansed—only Naaman the Syrian."
When they heard this, everyone in the synagogue was filled with rage.
They got up, drove him out of the town, and led him to the brow of the hill on which their town was built, intending to throw him off the cliff.
But he walked right through the middle of them and went on his way.
Then he went down to Capernaum, a town in Galilee, and he was teaching the people there on the Sabbath days.

versions.text: Then he went down to Capernaum, a town in Galilee, and he taught the people on the Sabbath.
versions.explanation: The periphrastic imperfect (ἦν διδάσκων) with the plural ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν indicates repeated, customary teaching on successive Sabbaths, not a single occasion.

text: They were amazed at his teaching, because his word carried authority.
In the synagogue there was a man possessed by the spirit of an unclean demon, and he cried out at the top of his voice,
"Ha! What do you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are—the Holy One of God!"
But Jesus rebuked him: "Be silent, and come out of him!" Then the demon threw the man down in front of them all and came out of him without doing him any harm.
Astonishment came over them all, and they said to one another, "What kind of message is this? With authority and power he gives orders to the unclean spirits, and out they come!"

versions.text: Astonishment came over them all, and they said to one another, "What is this word? With authority and power he gives orders to the unclean spirits, and out they come!"
versions.explanation: "What is this word?" is a wooden rendering that sounds unnatural when read aloud; λόγος here means the utterance or message he speaks, and the exclamation is one of wonder at its character.

text: And the report about him spread to every place in the surrounding region.
Leaving the synagogue, he went to Simon's house. Simon's mother-in-law was suffering from a high fever, and they asked him to help her.
He stood over her, rebuked the fever, and it left her. She got up at once and began to serve them.
At sunset, all who had anyone sick with various diseases brought them to him, and he laid his hands on each one of them and healed them.

versions.text: At sunset, all those who had friends sick with various diseases brought them to him, and he laid his hands on each one of them and healed them.
versions.explanation: The Greek says simply "as many as had any who were sick"; the word "friends" is an addition that narrows the sense and excludes family members and household servants, who are in fact the more likely referents.

text: Demons also came out of many, shouting, "You are the Son of God!" But he rebuked them and would not let them speak, because they knew he was the Christ.
At daybreak he left and went to a deserted place. The crowds went looking for him, and when they found him they tried to keep him from leaving.
But he said to them, "I must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns as well, because that is why I was sent."

And he kept on preaching in the synagogues of Judea.[^1]

[^1]: Some manuscripts read "of Galilee."

versions.text: And so he went on preaching in the synagogues of Judea.
versions.explanation: The Greek has only the simple connective καί; "And so" adds an inferential/causal nuance not present in the text. "He kept on preaching" preserves the continuous force of the periphrastic imperfect (ἦν κηρύσσων) while reading smoothly aloud.

versions.text: And he kept on preaching in the synagogues of Judea.
versions.explanation: There is a well-known textual variant here ("Galilee" instead of "Judea"), and since the preceding narrative is set in Galilee, a brief footnote would help hearers and readers understand the geographic reference.
